post.caption: Around 1865, Khande Rao Gaekwad, the Maharaja of Baroda, ordered a carpet of pearls. It was meant as a gift for the tomb of the Prophet in Medina. The base is silk and deer hide, and more than a million pearls from the Gulf cover it, with three large diamond rosettes in the center and hundreds of carats of diamonds in all. It measures 2.64 meters by 1.74 meters. The Maharaja died in 1870 before it could be sent, so it never left Baroda. Today it is the centerpiece of the National Museum of Qatar.
